title: Resistivity; EMF and internal resistance
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for CCEA A-level Physics (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EL04-1#t2 term and clue written for the game; EL04-uk1#t2 term and clue written for the game; EL04-uk1#t4 term and clue written for the game; EL04-1#t1 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EL04-1#N.4, EL04-uk1#N.3, EL08-1#N.3, EL04-1#N.6a, EL04-uk1#N.10, EL08-1#N.5a, EL04-1#N.10a, EL04-uk1#N.12, EL08-1#N.7a, EL08-1#N.10.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Resistance
items.clue: Quantity proportional to the length of a wire and to 1/A.

items.label: Crocodile clip
items.clue: Sliding connector that sets the length of wire being tested.

items.label: Voltmeter
items.clue: Instrument connected across the chosen length of wire, giving V for R = V/I.

items.label: Resistivity
items.clue: Property ρ that depends only on the material and its temperature, not on its shape.

questions.stem: A uniform copper wire is cut into two pieces of equal length. How do the resistance and the resistivity of one piece compare with those of the original wire?

options.text: Its resistance and its resistivity are both halved.
Its resistance and its resistivity are both the same.
Its resistance is the same, but its resistivity is halved.
Its resistance is halved; its resistivity is unchanged.

questions.stem: A student plots R against length for a uniform wire of diameter 0.40 mm. The best-fit line has a gradient of 4.0 Ω m⁻¹ and crosses the R axis at 0.30 Ω. What is the resistivity of the wire?
questions.explanation: A = π(0.40 × 10⁻³)²/4 = 1.26 × 10⁻⁷ m². ρ = gradient × A = 4.0 × 1.26 × 10⁻⁷ = 5.0 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m. The 0.30 Ω intercept (contact resistance) does not affect the gradient.

questions.stem: A battery with an internal resistance of 0.50 Ω drives a current of 0.60 A through a lamp, and an ideal voltmeter across the battery's terminals reads 4.2 V. The lamp is then disconnected, so that only the voltmeter remains connected across the battery. What does the voltmeter now read?
questions.explanation: emf = terminal potential difference + Ir = 4.2 + 0.60 × 0.50 = 4.5 V. With no current, the voltmeter reads the emf.

questions.stem: A copper cable has length 5.0 m and diameter 1.0 mm. The resistivity of copper is 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m. What is the resistance of the cable?
A cable is made from a ceramic superconductor with a critical temperature of 92 K. Which statement is correct?

options.text: It needs liquid helium (4 K), since every superconductor must be close to absolute zero.
Liquid nitrogen (77 K) keeps it superconducting, so it can carry a current with no heating.
It superconducts at room temperature, since 92 is well above zero.
At 77 K its resistivity is very small but not zero, so it still heats slightly.

questions.explanation: Right. 77 K is below 92 K, so its resistivity is zero: no energy is transferred as heat, however large the current.

questions.stem: A battery of emf 9.0 V and internal resistance 0.50 Ω is connected to a 4.0 Ω resistor. What is the terminal potential difference of the battery?

Wire X has resistance R and is made of a material of resistivity ρ. Wire Y is made of the same material at the same temperature, but it is half as long as X and has half the diameter of X. What are the resistance and the resistivity of wire Y?
questions.explanation: R ∝ length ÷ area: the length factor is ½ and the area factor is ¼, so R_Y = (½ ÷ ¼)R = 2R. Same material and temperature, so the same ρ.

questions.stem: An unlabelled wire has a mean diameter of 0.32 mm. Its resistance between the clips is 1.72 Ω at a length of 0.20 m and 5.37 Ω at 0.80 m. Resistivities: copper 1.7 × 10⁻⁸ Ω m; iron 1.0 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m; constantan 4.9 × 10⁻⁷ Ω m; nichrome 1.1 × 10⁻⁶ Ω m. Which metal is the wire most likely made of?
Cells P and Q have the same emf. P has a smaller internal resistance than Q. Each cell is connected in turn to the same lamp. Which statement is correct?

options.text: The lamp is equally bright with each, as both cells have the same emf.
The terminal pd is larger with P, as less pd is lost inside P.
The terminal pd is larger with Q, as more of the emf is across its resistance.
The current is the same with each, as the lamp alone sets the current.

questions.explanation: Current = emf/(R + r) is larger with P, but lost volts Ir is still smaller, so terminal pd = emf − Ir is larger and the lamp brighter.

questions.stem: A battery of internal resistance r is connected to an external resistor whose resistance equals r. The external resistor is then replaced by one of resistance 2r. How does the potential difference across the terminals of the battery change?

options.text: It stays equal to its first value.
It rises to 2 times its first value.
It falls to 2/3 of its first value.
It increases to 4/3 of its first value.
